model_annotation: Figure 4 illustrates the performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on the BioMedLM model, where “Base” denotes the LLM without editing. The x-axis represents the “Co-occurrence Number,” displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10¹ to 10⁴, with tick labels at 10¹, 10², 10³, and 10⁴. The y-axis shows “ACC (%)”, ranging linearly from 40% to 65%, with major tick marks every 5 percentage points. Six distinct lines are plotted, each corresponding to a different editing method: Base (black solid line with circle markers), FT (red solid line with square markers), MEMIT (green solid line with triangle markers), IKE (blue solid line with diamond markers), and ROME (purple solid line with inverted triangle markers). All lines show a generally increasing trend in accuracy as co-occurrence number increases. The Base model starts at approximately 42% ACC at 10¹ and rises to about 50% at 10⁴. FT begins near 45% and ends near 55%. MEMIT starts around 47% and reaches approximately 60%. IKE begins at ~44% and ends near 56%. ROME starts at ~46% and climbs to ~62%. Across all co-occurrence levels, ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, followed by MEMIT, while Base consistently performs the lowest.
